Theme

Town, shops & places

serve verb

at table

also can I help you?, wait on, serve (food), serve up

classical

ministrō, ministrāre

verb, first conjugation

serve at table

Other words

  • appōnō, appōnere, apposuī, appositum — serve up, set food before someone

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 2.4.69: adposita sit cēna (Lewis & Short); Traupman 68, 73

    Lewis & Short: “freq. as t. t. of food, dishes, to serve up, set before one”. Ministrāre is to wait on the person; appōnere is to put the dish on the table.

  • serviō, servīre, servīvī, servītum — be a slave to (not “serve at table”)

    verb, fourth conjugation · avoid · classical · Traupman 68, 73

    Traupman gives servīre for serving a person at table (Possumne tibi nunc servīre?); classically it means to be a slave or to be devoted to someone (Lewis & Short). A waiter ministrat.

Examples

  • Possumne tibi ministrāre?

    Can I help you?Traupman 67

  • Appōnam cibum quam prīmum.

    I’ll serve your meal as soon as I can.Traupman 68

See also waiter, restaurant.
